question: Audit whether the global Xi coefficient properties needed by H799 are known, provable from standard facts, or a new bottleneck.

sources.title: Jensen Polynomials for the Riemann Xi Function
sources.authors: Michael Griffin, Ken Ono, Larry Rolen, Jesse Thorner, Zachary Tripp, Ian Wagner
sources.use: Positivity of gamma(n), Polya/Jensen setup, global hyperbolicity for d<=3, effective eventual hyperbolicity for fixed degree.

sources.title: Jensen polynomials for the Riemann zeta function and other sequences
sources.authors: Michael Griffin, Ken Ono, Larry Rolen, Don Zagier
sources.use: Asymptotic Hermite modeling and eventual fixed-degree Jensen hyperbolicity; useful but not a direct global ratio-log-convexity proof.

sources.title: Zeros of Jensen polynomials and asymptotics for the Riemann xi function
sources.use: Detailed asymptotic expansions for xi Taylor coefficients and related quantities; relevant for eventual tail estimates.

sources.title: Jensen polynomials are not a plausible route to proving the Riemann Hypothesis
sources.use: Caution that Jensen asymptotics and eventual hyperbolicity should not be treated as RH-level evidence.

covered.adjacent_log_concavity_a_n: Covered if using the cited global d=2 Jensen/Turan result for gamma(n); factorial normalization strengthens the inequality by (n+1)/n.
covered.eventual_tail_smallness: Follows qualitatively from entire radius plus positive nonincreasing ratios, but no explicit cutoff was extracted.

bottleneck.source_status: Not found as a direct theorem in the primary sources checked.

decision: H799 remains a viable local-global lemma route, but H800 identifies ratio log-convexity of R_n as the hard unsourced bottleneck. Do not claim H798 globally until this is proved or replaced.
not_proved: Global q_{n+1}>=q_n for normalized Xi coefficient ratios.
Explicit analytic cutoff for the H799 tail bound.
The H798 family for all m.

next_target.name: H801 ratio-log-convexity attack
next_target.statement: Derive q_{n+1}>=q_n from an integral representation, a coefficient asymptotic with explicit remainder, or invalidate it with a higher-precision coefficient audit beyond H784.
